heroCommands.comment: Chat with a model from Hugging Face

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: llama.cpp runs large language models efficiently in C and C++ on a wide range of hardware, from laptops to cloud servers. It can download a model from Hugging Face and chat with it, or serve it through an OpenAI-compatible API with a built-in chat app.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running language models usually needs heavy Python stacks and big GPUs. llama.cpp aims for minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on many kinds of hardware, and it powers many other local AI tools.
whoFor: Developers running models locally with minimal setup
People with modest hardware who want local AI
Engineers embedding LLM inference in apps
Tool builders who need a fast inference engine
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for lightweight, fast local inference with GGUF models and an OpenAI-compatible server. For a more beginner-friendly wrapper, Ollama builds on it.
requirements: Enough RAM or VRAM for the model

overview: llama.cpp is built on the ggml tensor library. Its goal is LLM and multimodal model inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance, locally and in the cloud.

After installing, llama cli -hf downloads a GGUF model from Hugging Face and opens a chat session, including vision models. llama serve starts an OpenAI-compatible API server, and Llama Chat, a built-in chat app, can run against it.

You can install with a one-line script, use Docker, download pre-built binaries from the releases page or build from source. Documentation covers multi-GPU use, Android builds, text-to-speech models, grammars and performance tips. It is MIT licensed.
